rounds.text: Despite recent growth metrics, the business carries significant operational vulnerabilities and macro risks highlighted by management. The PU segment faces direct competitive pressure from cheap imports originating from China [E88]. Furthermore, geopolitical conflicts and trade policies have created major operational friction, including a fourfold surge in export shipping costs due to the Gulf War situation [E81], and delays in international plant expansion decisions driven by West Asia conflicts and Trump tariffs [E87]. Conceded: the company maintains high historical return on equity, a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.01x, and strong profitability metrics [E9, E37]. However, earnings growth has already shown signs of deceleration according to screening signals [E65], and domestic footwear demand was notably muted due to sharp increases in sole and raw material prices [E74]. Additionally, historical performance reveals high cyclicality with a severe peak-to-trough drawdown of -77.1% [E53], alongside volatile raw material costs that have fluctuated sharply [E82].

Conceded: the PU segment faces competitive pressure from cheap imports originating from China [E88], export shipping costs increased fourfold during the quarter due to the Gulf War [E81], and geopolitical issues have delayed international plant location decisions [E87]. However, the bear's focus on operational friction overlooks the immediate tangible offsets, such as new OEM supply orders from the U.S.A. that have already started contributing positively to export sales revenue and overall profitability [E84]. Furthermore, management explicitly expects this positive growth momentum in exports and U.S. automotive business to continue over the next two to three years, targeting a 60% to 70% increase [E72, E76]. Conceded: domestic footwear demand was muted due to sharp raw material price increases [E74], and raw material situations have been volatile [E82]. Despite these hurdles, operating margins are expanding and trending upward over the last five years [E30, E32], capacity utilization sits at a healthy 75% to 78% [E83], and an additional production capacity of 5 lakh meters is scheduled to start by the end of the financial year [E77].

Conceded: U.S. OEM orders have started contributing to revenue [E84], and capacity utilization is between 75% and 78% [E83]. However, citing these offsets ignores the severe macroeconomic headwinds and volatility acknowledged by management, including raw material price swings and a fourfold surge in export shipping costs caused by the Gulf War [E81, E82]. While the bull points to planned capacity additions of 5 lakh meters by early 2027 [E77], this minor expansion occurs against a backdrop of domestic footwear demand being muted by rising material costs [E74], and domestic institutional holdings dropping sharply from 8.67% in Dec 2023 to 2.94% in Sep 2026 [E43]. Furthermore, reliance on multi-year export projections [E72, E76] must be weighed against management's own admissions that geopolitical risks, potential Trump tariffs, and West Asia conflicts have outright delayed the location decisions for any international plant expansion [E87]. Finally, the screen engine itself explicitly flags that earnings growth is decelerating [E65], suggesting that the optimism surrounding margin trends and forward-looking growth targets runs ahead of near-term structural pressures.

Conceded: export shipping costs surged 4x due to the Gulf War [E81], and geopolitical issues and potential tariffs have delayed international plant location decisions [E87]. However, the bear's focus on macro volatility ignores the company's robust operational reality, such as current capacity utilization sitting comfortably between 75% and 78% [E83] alongside an expanding production capacity of 5 lakh meters slated for early 2027 [E77]. Conceded: domestic institutional holdings fell from 8.67% to 2.94% [E43] and domestic footwear demand was muted [E74], but foreign institutions increased their stake to 5.28% [E42], resulting in overall positive money flow [E44]. Furthermore, U.S. OEM supply orders are actively contributing to export revenue and profitability [E84], supporting management's targeted 15% growth outlook [E73] and projected 60% to 70% increase in U.S. business over the next three years [E72].

The bull cites healthy capacity utilization between 75% and 78% [E83] and an incoming expansion of 5 lakh meters by early 2027 [E77], but ignores that management has delayed its major international plant location decision entirely due to geopolitical uncertainty and potential Trump tariffs [E87]. Conceded: foreign institutional holdings rose [E42], but this ignores the sharp exodus of domestic institutions dropping their stake from 8.67% to 2.94% [E43], signaling a serious split in professional conviction. Furthermore, while the bull leans on management's 15% growth outlook [E73] and U.S. projections [E72], screens explicitly flag that earnings growth is actively decelerating [E65], matching management's admissions of a volatile raw material environment [E82] and 4x higher shipping costs from the Gulf War [E81]. Finally, the reliance on recent U.S. OEM contributions [E84] overlooks the company's own warnings that prior quarter margins were abnormally inflated by transient foreign exchange movements [E80] rather than sustainable core expansion.

evidence.fact: Management expects US business to increase by 60% to 70% in the next three years.
evidence.quote: Sir we have already told that our US business will increase and next in next three years the business will almost be if not double at least 60%, 70% our US business will increase, right? In terms of US automotive.

evidence.quote: So we have kept potential outlook for 15% growth in the coming year also.

evidence.quote: So obviously, the market was muted in the footwear segment.

evidence.fact: Management noted that the recent FTA signed by India is a very positive move that will improve cost effectiveness and customer procurement sentiments from India.
evidence.quote: I think so it's a very positive move for India. Definitely, we will be more effective in terms of cost. The sentiments of the customers to procure from India will definitely increase.

evidence.fact: The positive growth momentum in exports is expected to continue for the next two to three years.
evidence.quote: And this increased momentum is expected to continue in the next 2, 3 years.

evidence.fact: The company has ordered a new line for its current premises with production expected to start towards the end of the financial year between February and March 2027, adding an additional production capacity of 5 lakh meters.
evidence.quote: So we should be able to start our production by -- towards the end of this financial year, somewhere between February, March 2027. So we'll have an additional production capacity of 5 lakh meters.

evidence.fact: Management stated that if they decide to put up a new facility, the capex in the next 2 years would be INR250 crores.
evidence.quote: So, if that happens, then in the next 2 years, you will have a capex of 250 crores. Yes, it will be additional.

evidence.fact: It will take approximately two years for the proposed plant to start after a final decision is made.
evidence.quote: So once the decision is taken, it takes approximately 2 years for the plant to start.

evidence.fact: Management stated that the previous quarter's margin was abnormally high due to an abnormal increase in foreign exchange rates.
evidence.quote: But last quarter, it was abnormally high because of foreign exchange increase in -- abnormally high increase in foreign exchange rates. So that was a onetime increase basically.

evidence.fact: Management reported that shipping costs for exports increased 4x during the quarter due to the Gulf War situation.
evidence.quote: It's 4x higher, the shipment cost was increased.

evidence.fact: Management noted that raw material prices went up sharply, followed by a fall and subsequent increases, creating a volatile situation.
evidence.quote: The prices went up very sharply, then there was a fall in prices of some raw materials. Then again, the prices went up again. So, it's been a very volatile situation.

evidence.fact: Current capacity utilization is reported to be between 75% and 78%.
evidence.quote: So, we are utilizing somewhere between 75% to 78%.

evidence.fact: Management received good OEM supply orders from the U.S.A., which have started contributing to export sales revenue and profitability.

evidence.fact: Management has not taken any final decision regarding a share buyback.
evidence.quote: So for buyback, we have not taken the call.

evidence.fact: The PU segment faces headwinds from cheap imports from China.
evidence.quote: A lot of cheap imports are coming from China.
